Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System (PACNS)

candidates.name: Cerebral Vasculitis
support_spans: Emergent cerebral angiography revealed diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries and their branches, along with diffuse luminal narrowing and dysplastic changes in the right distal vertebral artery and basilar trunk, consistent with cerebral angiitis
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and cerebral angiography results are consistent with cerebral vasculitis.

candidates.name: Neurosarcoidosis
support_spans: Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated T2 hyperintense lesions in the frontal, left parietal, and left occipital lobes with leptomeningeal enhancement
contradict_spans: Tests of CSF—including Gram stain and culture, PCR for herpes simplex virus and enteroviruses, cryptococcal antigen, and fungal cultures—were negative
candidates.why: The patient's neuroimaging results and clinical presentation could be consistent with neurosarcoidosis, but the negative CSF tests make it less likely.

candidates.name: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
support_spans: Emergent cerebral angiography revealed diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries and their branches, along with diffuse luminal narrowing and dysplastic changes in the right distal vertebral artery and basilar trunk, consistent with cerebral angiitis
candidates.why: The patient's cerebral angiography results are consistent with primary central nervous system vasculitis.

candidates.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with CNS involvement
support_spans: A positive antinuclear antibody titer (>1:320) with a nucleolar pattern
contradict_spans: negative anti-centromere antibody, and negative anti-Scl-70 antibody
candidates.why: The patient's positive ANA and clinical presentation could be consistent with SLE with CNS involvement, but the negative specific autoantibodies make it less likely.

candidates.name: Relapsing Polychondritis
contradict_spans: A forearm skin biopsy demonstrated increased dermal collagen and superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltration
candidates.why: There is no clear evidence to support relapsing polychondritis in this patient.

support_spans: cerebral angiography revealed diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries and their branches
